GPU instances can accelerate the neural-network computation in DeepAR compared with CPU-only training, subject to workload size and batch configuration.

302: Recall is the proportion of actual abnormalities detected. When avoiding missed abnormalities is the explicit priority, compare the recall values.
Recall of 0.60 misses 40% of actual abnormalities. Its stronger precision does not compensate for that under the stated detection priority.
Recall of 0.98 detects the highest fraction of actual abnormalities among the options, missing about 2%. The lower precision implies more false alarms, which remain a separate operational tradeoff.
Recall of 0.90 detects fewer true abnormalities than the 0.98 alternative, despite a somewhat higher precision.
Precision of 0.98 makes alarms reliable, but recall of 0.80 still misses one fifth of actual abnormalities. It does not maximize detection probability.

308: PCA is sensitive to feature scale, so numeric variables with different units should be scaled before their covariance structure is used for dimensionality reduction.
Applying PCA directly can let large-range variables dominate the components even when their larger numerical scale does not imply greater predictive importance.

Min-max scaling places the variables on comparable ranges before PCA compresses their correlated information. Fit both preprocessing steps on training data only, and validate the retained component count.
Standard scaling is reasonable, but deleting correlated features first can discard information that PCA is designed to combine. That extra removal is not required by the task.
Weakly correlated features may contain valuable independent signal. Removing them before PCA can unnecessarily damage regression performance.
